status: Locally specified before candidate performance measurement. Known regression fixtures disclosed; fresh families reserved until one locked run. Not public preregistration.
question: Does removing automatic score decay improve adaptation without losing reversal/return performance?
motivation: The exact switch control finds +2.04 HP [0.33,3.83] after diverse pretraining, below the practical 3 HP threshold. A diagnostic identified harmful probability shifts but did not establish decay as their cause.
change: Only POLICY_CONFIG.decay differs: 0.025 versus 0. All rewards, learning rate, exploration, temperature, update cap, representation, seeds and combat abilities are unchanged. Sampled actions still update at learning_rate=0.22; no-decay is not permanent memory.

fresh_behaviors.burst-patrol: Navigate a four-point perimeter, stop for the last 35% of each leg interval. Direction switch reverses waypoint order.
fresh_behaviors.threat-retreat: Approach visible enemies until close; retreat when visible windups or nearby bullets signal danger, with signed lateral motion. Direction switch reverses lateral motion.

sensory_constraints: Same delayed restricted observations, aiming noise, decision cadence and ability bounds as synthetic v1. Public geometry only; no tactic, policy, hidden positions or enemy RNG. Controllers are hand-authored and do not learn.
branching: Train each variant separately. For legacy cases fork online/frozen immediately after training. For synthetic cases train diverse for 48, repeat for 12, then fork online/frozen at the exact switch. Continue the online branch, then fork again at the exact return. Each within-variant pair restores the identical snapshot including RNG. Never restore across configurations.
primary_endpoint: No-decay online minus original online damage, last four switch rounds, equal average of four fresh cases per seed. Compare algorithms under equal encounter histories; their actual sampled actions and observations may differ.

required: Fresh primary gain >=3 HP and paired 95% lower bound >0
Fresh no-decay switch online-minus-boundary-frozen >=3 HP and lower bound >0
Known legacy feint candidate-minus-original >=3 HP and lower bound >0
Known legacy feint candidate learning benefit mean >=0
No synthetic switch or return case, nor legacy reversal/cover, loses more than 3 HP mean versus original
gates.decision: All gates must pass for a further validation candidate; passing does not install a production change. Otherwise retain original. No sweep, retuning, extra seeds or early stopping based on outcomes.

uncertainty.scope: Paired percentile bootstrap over 12 seeds per suite; aggregate cases and rounds within seed. These are fixed authored families, not independent draws from all games. Secondary comparisons unadjusted.

budget.interpretation: Equal encounter histories per variant; record actual simulation steps and process CPU. No fixed-compute efficiency claim.

secondary: Per-case damage, player clear/death rates and duration
All choices, rewards, checkpoints, input fingerprints and geometry rejection records
limits: Neither decay nor lack of decay repairs missing joint-role credit or adds route memory.
Fresh behaviors/maps form a small prospective screen and become known regression fixtures after this run.
Direction changes are scripted, bots do not model or learn the enemy, and no human enjoyment is measured.
Reward, representation and runtime remain unchanged. No fixed-policy superiority claim is tested here.
Original and candidate are separately trained: the primary effect covers the complete configured learning history, not just post-switch decay.
Geometry validity and unit tests may run before the source freeze using non-evaluation seeds; no reserved combat may guide implementation.

demonstration.selection: Preselected before any measured candidate outcomes; show all four original/no-decay online/frozen conditions even if uneventful.
